submitted.rationale: Index 10 (Ag 0.4845 / V 0.5155) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 2.4e-7 A. That is 8× index 12 (Ag3VO4 region, 3e-8 A). Index 10 is the most V-rich composition in the library and sits near AgVO3, which MACE puts on the hull and MEGNet gives an HSE gap of about 2.9–3.0 eV, low enough to absorb the 3.22 eV light.

rejected.reason: Measured 3e-8 A. Ag3VO4 region; MEGNet predicts a near-zero gap for this phase, which I treated as unreliable.
Measured -8e-8 A even though it is near AgVO3 stoichiometry. Its XRD showed only substrate peaks, so the film may be amorphous or poorly crystallized.
Not measured because the budget ran out. The GP suggested it (mean 1.2e-7 A, below index 10).

consultations.verdict: MACE puts Ag3VO4 (mp-19412) near the hull (0.023 eV/atom), which supports that it can form at index 12 (Ag 0.745). The MEGNet HSE gap of about 0 eV conflicts with the experimental gap of about 2.2 eV, so I treat it as unreliable. Overall this is support: a stable, visible-absorbing Ag3VO4 phase should absorb the 3.22 eV illumination.

MACE puts AgVO3 (mp-559736) essentially on the hull (0.012 eV/atom). Earlier, MEGNet gave it an HSE gap of 2.9 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy. That means it can absorb the light and a gap this wide can drive the oxidation. This supports measuring the V-rich end at index 10 (Ag 0.48), which is the composition closest to AgVO3.

MEGNet gives the AgVO3 polymorph mp-624691 an HSE gap of 2.97 eV, which the 3.22 eV illumination can excite. This is consistent with the AgVO3-region hit at index 10 (2.4e-7 A). Index 5 (Ag 0.525) is next to index 10 and closest to exact AgVO3 stoichiometry, so this supports measuring it.
